\chapter{Gifts, Welcomes, Apologies}
\label{ch:ta-gifts-welcomes}
\hlchaptermodality{99}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can offer a drink, name a gift given with affection, welcome formally, ask forgiveness, and say don't worry.}

\section[kuṭiyuṅkaḷ]{\ta{குடியுங்கள்} (kuṭiyuṅkaḷ) — please drink}

\label{lesson:TA-C99-drink}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for please come in, then the Tamil for please eat.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{குடியுங்கள்}}
\textbf{\ta{குடியுங்கள்}} (\emph{kuṭiyuṅkaḷ}) — \textquotedblleft{}please drink\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\ta{தண்ணீர்} \ta{குடியுங்கள்}} — \textquotedblleft{}please have some water\textquotedblright{}.

Look at \textbf{\ta{தண்ணீர்}}: it is the thing being drunk, and it carries no \textbf{-\ta{ஐ}}. A thing can do without the ending that a person must have.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Food, and now drink.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kuṭiyuṅkaḷ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kuṭiyuṅkaḷ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{taṇṇīr kuṭiyuṅkaḷ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for please come in, then the Tamil for please eat, then say \emph{kuṭiyuṅkaḷ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{குடியுங்கள்} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Please drink\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[aṉpaḷippu]{\ta{அன்பளிப்பு} (aṉpaḷippu) — a gift given with affection}

\label{lesson:TA-C99-present}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for please eat, then the Tamil for please drink.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{அன்பளிப்பு}}
\textbf{\ta{அன்பளிப்பு}} (\emph{aṉpaḷippu}) — \textquotedblleft{}a present\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}a giving of love\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\ta{அன்பு}} is \textquotedblleft{}love\textquotedblright{}; \textbf{\ta{அளிப்பு}} is \textquotedblleft{}a giving\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\ta{பரிசு}} can be a prize; \textbf{\ta{அன்பளிப்பு}} is always from the heart.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A second word for gift, with love in it.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aṉpaḷippu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aṉpaḷippu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{aṉpaḷippu}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for please eat, then the Tamil for please drink, then say \emph{aṉpaḷippu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{அன்பளிப்பு} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A gift given with affection\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[nalvaravu]{\ta{நல்வரவு} (nalvaravu) — welcome (formal)}

\label{lesson:TA-C99-welcomeformal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for please drink, then the Tamil for a present.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{நல்வரவு}}
\textbf{\ta{நல்வரவு}} (\emph{nalvaravu}) — \textquotedblleft{}welcome\textquotedblright{}, the formal word, literally \textquotedblleft{}good arrival\textquotedblright{}.

You will see it on banners and doorways; \textbf{\ta{வாருங்கள்}} is what you say aloud.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The written welcome.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nalvaravu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nalvaravu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{nalvaravu}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for please drink, then the Tamil for a present, then say \emph{nalvaravu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{நல்வரவு} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Welcome (formal)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[maṉṉittuviṭuṅkaḷ]{\ta{மன்னித்துவிடுங்கள்} (maṉṉittuviṭuṅkaḷ) — please forgive me}

\label{lesson:TA-C99-forgive}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for a present, then the Tamil for a formal welcome.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{மன்னித்துவிடுங்கள்}}
\textbf{\ta{மன்னித்துவிடுங்கள்}} (\emph{maṉṉittuviṭuṅkaḷ}) — \textquotedblleft{}please forgive me\textquotedblright{}.

It is fuller and more earnest than \textbf{\ta{மன்னிக்கவும்}}: for a real mistake, not a bumped elbow.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A fuller apology.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{maṉṉittuviṭuṅkaḷ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{maṉṉittuviṭuṅkaḷ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{maṉṉittuviṭuṅkaḷ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for a present, then the Tamil for a formal welcome, then say \emph{maṉṉittuviṭuṅkaḷ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{மன்னித்துவிடுங்கள்} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Please forgive me\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[kavalaippaṭātīrkaḷ]{\ta{கவலைப்படாதீர்கள்} (kavalaippaṭātīrkaḷ) — don't worry}

\label{lesson:TA-C99-dontworry}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for a formal welcome, then the Tamil for please forgive me.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{கவலைப்படாதீர்கள்}}
\textbf{\ta{கவலைப்படாதீர்கள்}} (\emph{kavalaippaṭātīrkaḷ}) — \textquotedblleft{}please don't worry\textquotedblright{}.

It is \textbf{\ta{கவலை}}, \textquotedblleft{}worry\textquotedblright{}, with \textbf{\ta{படு}}, \textquotedblleft{}to suffer\textquotedblright{}, and the respectful don't.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Drink, a present, a welcome, forgiveness, and don't worry.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kavalaippaṭātīrkaḷ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kavalaippaṭātīrkaḷ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{kavalaippaṭātīrkaḷ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for a formal welcome, then the Tamil for please forgive me, then say \emph{kavalaippaṭātīrkaḷ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{கவலைப்படாதீர்கள்} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Don't worry\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
